scene: Day 365, a huge shining bay of wet sand at low tide. The beige coach crawls across the flats toward a small hump of an island with an old stone fort, its horn blaring, followed by a long line of hundreds of green walkers strung out behind it across the sand, while thin bright lines of seawater creep in from the edges. In the foreground, at the top of the beach, Patch (white round head, orange bandage above his right eye, orange backpack) leans out of the white truck's window, eyes huge, one sweat drop, watching the tide come in. Tense because the sea is closing and Vera and Wes are still on the bus.

Day 362, midday, a low hill above a long pale beach and a flat shining sea. A long stone causeway runs out from the beach to a dark rock with little houses and a white lighthouse, and along it, standing knee-deep, waist-deep and chest-deep in the sea, a long dark line of green walkers faces the lighthouse, hundreds more crowding the beach behind them; at the end of the causeway there is no gate at all. Nora (round white head, purple band on her right forearm, teal backpack) holds up a postcard of the same lighthouse in front of the real view. In the foreground, Patch (white round head, orange bandage above his right eye, orange backpack) stands beside the white truck, eyes huge, one sweat drop. Tense because the dead are already halfway to the rock.
